title: What's New: Cloud for Sovereignty (2026 release wave 1)

chapters.title: Microsoft's Five Digital Commitments for Europe
Cloud for Sovereignty Overview and Access Controls
Role-Based Access Control and Privileged Identity Management
Sovereignty Controls and Geographic Data Placement

features.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
features.description: Enforces layered access through security groups at environment level, Entra ID groups, entitlements, and permission sets to determine what users can access within Business Central environments.

features.name: Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
features.description: Allows customers to grant elevated access on a temporary and reviewed basis through Entra roles, security group memberships, and conditional access policies for Business Central.

features.name: Granular Delegated Admin Permissions (GDAP)
features.description: Enables customers to approve Entra role assignments that partners need to access customer environments, using the Dynamics 365 Business Central administrator role as the recommended least privileged role.

features.name: Isolated SQL Database per Environment
features.description: Each Business Central environment runs as its own dedicated isolated SQL database with no data commingling between environments.

features.name: Encryption at Rest
features.description: Business Central environments are encrypted at rest by default using Microsoft-owned keys, with the option for customers to use their own encryption keys (customer-managed encryption key).
caveats: Customers can rotate security keys monthly for compliance reasons
Customer-managed keys enable revoking Microsoft access to data

features.name: Dynamics 365 Business Central Service Tag
features.description: Represents a group of IP addresses from which traffic of a Business Central environment may come, allowing customers to secure integrations via firewall rules.

features.name: Environment Localization and Geographic Data Placement
features.description: Customers can select environment localization which determines the Azure geography where the Business Central database resides, independent of the tenant home geo.
caveats: Region is where the service runs
Availability zone protects against local failures

features.name: Azure Region Pairing and Backup
features.description: Data centers are organized in paired regions with automatic backups and failover protection to ensure high availability and protect data during disruptive events.

features.name: Purview Audit and Monitoring
features.description: Microsoft-wide service allowing customers to audit activity on Business Central services and environments, including activities in the admin center requiring admin privileges, for forensic investigations and compliance.

features.name: Change Logs and Field Monitoring
features.description: Built-in Business Central functionality allowing customers to audit and monitor activity, tracking who accessed and changed data and environment settings.

features.name: Just-In-Time (JIT) Access Controls
features.description: Microsoft-side access control mechanism where engineers must justify, request, and obtain approval for temporary time-limited access to customer databases to investigate or mitigate support requests, with all activity logged.
caveats: Default is no Microsoft employee access to customer data
Access only authorized for limited time
All engineering activity is logged for audit

features.name: Customer Lockbox
features.description: Feature allowing customer admins to approve or reject Microsoft engineer requests for access to customer data when needed to investigate or mitigate support issues, providing customer control over emergency access.
caveats: Customer approval required after internal Microsoft approval
